title: Dollar strengthens after a hotter-than-expected US inflation print
summary: The dollar rose 1.2% against a basket of currencies after US consumer prices increased 3.4% year on year, above forecasts.

articles.title: Dollar strengthens after a hotter-than-expected US inflation print
articles.text:
The US dollar gained 1.2% against a basket of major currencies on Thursday after data showed consumer prices rose 3.4% year on year in September, above the 3.1% expected by economists.

Traders scaled back bets on a Federal Reserve rate cut in December. Sterling fell 0.9% against the dollar and the euro lost 0.8%.

Exporters that bill clients in dollars benefit from a stronger dollar, while importers paying in dollars face higher costs.
